title: Customer-managed cryptographic operations guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects pragmatic operational guidance for customer-managed keys (tenant-owned keys) across Redwood’s environments. It specifically ties key lifecycle operations to RBAC v2 controls, audit record formats required for downstream evidence automation, and recommended SIEM mappings so the security team and compliance reviewers can reconstruct any rotation/escrow event end-to-end.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to customer-managed keys used to encrypt customer data at rest (disk volumes, object storage E2E encryption, DB column encryption).
- Covers hardware-backed keys (HSMs), cloud KMS keys under customer-managed key policies, and tenant-supplied keys uploaded via the onboarding handshake (customer key import).
- Assumes RBAC v2 is enforced for all key operations; service principal actions must be scoped to least privilege.
- Intended to support evidence collection for audits (SOC2, PCI-like controls).

High-level goals:
1) Ensure rotation and revocation operations are atomic and reconstructable.
2) Make evidence for every key lifecycle change available to SIEM and evidence automation pipelines with minimal manual work.
3) Provide clear fallbacks to HSM-backed keys for emergency recovery while preserving customer isolation guarantees.

Operational roles (RBAC v2 mapping, short):
- role:crypto-admin -> permissions: key:create, key:rotate, key:revoke, key:import, audit:export
- role:crypto-operator -> permissions: key:rotate (scheduled only), key:view, logs:view
- role:service-account/key-agent -> permissions: crypt:encrypt, crypt:decrypt (scoped to key ids), key:cache-access
- role:compliance-reader -> permissions: audit:read, evidence:export

Notes: use attribute-based constraints for role:crypto-operator so rotations must be tied to a Jira changeid and not run ad-hoc. Example constraint: allowed_if jira_change IS NOT NULL.

Key onboarding handshake (tenant-supplied key flow):
1) Customer uploads key material (wrapped) via the onboarding API endpoint. Request must include: customer_id, key_alias, wrapping_kek_id (Redwood-managed), origin (hsm|cloud-kms|import), and onboarding_ticket (jira id).
2) System validates signature on upload and enqueues a validation job. Validation checks: key format, algorithm family, permitted key length, and allowed origins for the customer tier.
3) On successful validation: create a key record with status=ENABLED and initial_version metadata containing: uploaded_by (email), onboarding_ticket, upload_timestamp. Emit audit event: crypto.key.onboarded.
4) All onboarding events are required to have a corresponding evidence bundle in S3 and an index entry in the evidence DB used by the automation pipeline.

Rotation lifecycle and automation pattern (recommended):
- Rotation cadence: default 90d for symmetric tenant keys, 365d for asymmetric signing keys unless customer requests otherwise.
- Rotation must be orchestrated through the rotation service (not manual ops shell).
- Rotation job payload includes: key_id, initiated_by (user/service), jira_change_id, rotation_reason, preflight_checks (list), target_kek (if re-wrap).
- Preflight checks the rotation service performs: key active, no pending decryption jobs older than TTL, backup snapshot exists, replication healthy to other regions.
- Rotation steps (atomic outline):
  a) Lock key record (RBAC ensures only rotation service lock token can proceed).
  b) Export ephemeral rewrap token to HSM-proxy or KMS (implementation specific).
  c) Create new key_version and begin re-encrypt of active key material in background with traffic routing to old version until switch.
  d) Switch traffic to new version during a short maintenance window (feature flags if needed).
  e) Verify decrypts with a sample set (smoke tests).
  f) Mark previous versions as deprecated but retained for rollback within configured retention window.
  g) Emit final audit event crypto.key.rotated and create evidence package.

Emergency revocation / compromise flow (summary):
- Trigger via ticket:SEC-EMERG-REVOKE + call to 2-person approval (crypto-admin + oncall SRE).
- Immediate steps: mark key status=REVOKED, push invalidate caches to all key-agents, emit crypto.key.revoked event with justification and ticket id.
- For customer-managed keys, notify customer out-of-band with secure channel; provide evidence package and request re-onboarding if necessary.

Audit events and minimal schema (plaintext examples used by evidence automation):
- Event name: crypto.key.onboarded
  - timestamp: 2026-01-12T18:10:04Z
  - actor: aditi.rao@redwood.ai
  - key_id: key-cus-7921
  - origin: hsm
  - onboarding_ticket: SEC-3129
  - evidence_uri: s3://evidence-prod/customer-7921/onboard/2026-01-12.tar.gz

- Event name: crypto.key.rotated
  - timestamp: 2026-02-08T02:22:11Z
  - actor: rotation-service@redwood.ai
  - key_id: key-cus-7921
  - previous_version: v3
  - new_version: v4
  - jira_change_id: SEC-4089
  - preflight_status: PASSED
  - smoke_test_results: {passed:34, failed:0}
  - evidence_uri: s3://evidence-prod/customer-7921/rotate/2026-02-08.tar.gz

- Event name: crypto.key.revoked
  - timestamp: 2026-02-10T23:41:05Z
  - actor: marcus.chen@redwood.ai
  - key_id: key-cus-7921
  - reason: suspected-key-exfiltration
  - approval_ids: [PRIV-OP-22, PRIV-OP-23]
  - evidence_uri: s3://evidence-prod/customer-7921/revoke/2026-02-10.tar.gz

Note: evidence_uri points to the automated evidence exporter bundle that must contain: operation log (raw), signed statements from approval actors, replayable rewrap transcripts, and system snapshots (config, access lists).

SIEM export mapping (recommended fields to populate for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic):
- index: crypto_events (or existing security index)
- host: runtime-hostname
- sourcetype: redwood:crypto:event
- fields: event_name, timestamp, actor, key_id, origin, action, outcome, jira_change_id, evidence_uri, region, tenant_id
- parse rules: timestamp in ISO8601, actor normalized to email, key_id canonicalized to key-<type>-<shortid>
- retention policy: keep raw events for 3 years in cold storage; high-fidelity indexed fields for 1 year.

Automated evidence pipeline (integration points):
1) Event producer (rotation/onboard/revoke) emits signed JSON to the event bus (kafka-topic: crypto.audit.v1).
2) Evidence exporter (consumer) collects related artifacts from: operations logs, HSM audit journal, onboarding payload, snapshot of RBAC policy, and stores a tarball to evidence S3 bucket.
3) Indexer writes a compact metadata record to the evidence DB and triggers SIEM-forwarding lambda.
4) SIEM-forwarding lambda transforms the event to the canonical SIEM schema and pushes to configured destinations.
5) Compliance-runner can request replays for a time range which rehydrate evidence bundles for auditors.

Operational checklist (pre-rotation):
- [ ] Confirm jira_change_id exists and is approved
- [ ] Confirm backup snapshot of key-state is accessible and validated
- [ ] Ensure replication to DR region is healthy
- [ ] Validate there are no long-running decryption jobs older than configured TTL
- [ ] Run smoke tests against sample decrypts for the key
- [ ] Notify affected tenants if rotation window will cause transient errors

Post-rotation validation (automated):
- Verify 100% of traffic decrypts within latency SLO for a 10m sample window
- Confirm all microservices using the key have switched to new_version (via key-agent heartbeats)
- Confirm evidence tarball exists and index entry is searchable
- Close the rotation jira and attach evidence export id

HSM fallback and recovery patterns:
- Prefer HSM-backed wrapping/unwrap for tenant customer keys when customer requests hardware assurance.
- Keep a locked, auditable escrow only if contractually allowed. Escrow operations require multi-party signing and are restricted to role:crypto-admin with 2-of-3 approvers.
- For cross-region failover, use HSM-proxy rewrap (no export of raw key material) and document the proxy transcript in evidence bundle.

Open questions / follow-ups (work items):
- Q1: Do we want automated tenant notification for every rotation by default? (SEC-6123)
- Q2: Add field to audit schema to record key-policy-hash so drift can be detected automatically. (design spike assigned to Aditi)
- Q3: SLA for evidence delivery to customer after revocation (propose 72h).

Quick links / commands (ops):
- Rotation dry-run: scripts/rotation/dry_run.sh --key-id key-cus-XXX --jira SEC-XXXX
- Rewrap audit transcript export: scripts/evidence/export_rewrap.sh --bundle-id <id> --out /tmp
- Revoke API (internal): POST /internal/crypto/v1/keys/<id>/revoke {"actor":"<email>","ticket":"<jira>"}

Appendix: minimal JSON event example (one-line) for downstream consumers:
{"event_name":"crypto.key.rotated","timestamp":"2026-02-08T02:22:11Z","actor":"rotation-service@redwood.ai","key_id":"key-cus-7921","previous_version":"v3","new_version":"v4","jira_change_id":"SEC-4089","evidence_uri":"s3://evidence-prod/customer-7921/rotate/2026-02-08.tar.gz","outcome":"SUCCESS"}

Endnotes:
This is an operational living doc. If you make changes to rotation semantics or evidence contents, please update the Confluence playbook (confluence:SEC-CRYPTO-PLAYBOOK) and file a short PR (github:redwood/ops-scripts) with integration test updates.

Unresolved: the recommended retention windows for evidence are conservative; discuss cost tradeoffs with finance (jira:FIN-ev-retention).

-- Marcus (crypto ops)
